title: Inference at the inflection: unit economics flip favorable
body: We see AI inference cost per token declining ~70% over the next 12 months as model architectures, custom silicon, and lower-cost connectivity converge. The principal beneficiaries are not the hyperscalers themselves but the downstream enablers — connectivity silicon (CRDO), networking fabrics (ANET), and second-source GPU vendors (AMD). Inference cost deflation expands TAM rather than compressing margins because elasticity of demand exceeds 1 at current price points.

title: The Quiet Repricing of AI Inference
body: Conversations with three frontier-model engineering leads suggest that inference cost has fallen 4x in eighteen months and is set to fall further. The story is not that GPUs are cheaper — they aren't — but that connectivity overhead and memory bandwidth bottlenecks are being engineered out of the stack. Companies like Credo Technology and Arista are well positioned as the inference layer scales out laterally rather than vertically.

title: Inference deflation is the bull case nobody is pricing
body: I keep hearing the same thing from people building production AI systems: the cost curve is bending faster than anyone expected. This is great for application companies and for the picks-and-shovels names — connectivity, networking, even the second-tier GPU makers. The first-order beneficiary is not NVDA.

title: Japan Semiconductor: the second wave of fab capacity
body: Japan's semiconductor reindustrialization is entering a second leg as Rapidus, TSMC's Kumamoto JV, and Kioxia simultaneously add advanced capacity. Tokyo Electron is the largest beneficiary in the WFE supply chain. Advantest has effective monopoly share in advanced HBM test. Shin-Etsu Chemical's wafer business reaccelerates as new fab utilization comes online. The macro tailwind is yen weakness combined with subsidy-driven capex.

title: Tokyo Electron's order book signals secular Japan fab cycle
body: Tokyo Electron reported a record backlog driven by domestic demand from Rapidus and overseas customers expanding their Japanese footprint. The company's commentary on the conference call described Japan reindustrialization in semiconductor manufacturing as a 'multi-year structural cycle.' Suppliers including Advantest and Shin-Etsu Chemical are signaling similar order momentum.

title: Why Japan is back on the semiconductor map
body: After three decades of decline, Japanese semiconductor manufacturing is in the middle of a deliberate, state-backed reindustrialization. Rapidus' 2nm pilot line in Hokkaido, TSMC's expansion in Kumamoto, and a broader supply-chain ecosystem (Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Shin-Etsu Chemical) are converging into a coherent industrial policy outcome.

title: TSMC commentary cites Japan capacity expansion
body: On the Q1 2026 earnings call, TSMC management explicitly noted that capacity expansion in Japan is 'progressing on schedule' and is part of the company's strategy for geographic redundancy. This is a lagging acknowledgment — Japan reindustrialization has been visible in the supply chain for over a year, but a Mag-cap explicitly framing it on a public call typically signals the narrative has reached late-Strengthening or Consensus stage.

title: Japan semis are obvious — what's next?
body: Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Shin-Etsu — the Japan fab basket has been ripping for months. By the time it's on FinTwit it's no longer alpha. Where do you rotate?

title: Nuclear renaissance: SMR commercialization timelines compress
body: Hyperscaler power demand combined with grid-stability constraints is collapsing SMR commercialization timelines. We see BWXT, the sole US naval-grade reactor component manufacturer, as the cleanest leveraged play. Cameco benefits from the front end of the fuel cycle. Vistra Energy owns operating nuclear capacity that has become the scarcest asset class on the grid.

title: Hyperscalers sign first nuclear PPAs
body: Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta have each announced multi-year power-purchase agreements with operators of existing nuclear plants. The shift reflects rising data-center power requirements, particularly for AI training and inference, and the inability of intermittent renewable sources alone to meet round-the-clock demand at the scale required.

title: The grid problem is a nuclear opportunity
body: AI-driven electricity demand is the most underappreciated story in markets. The grid cannot accommodate it without firm dispatchable power, and natural gas faces emissions constraints. SMR commercialization, currently scheduled for the late 2020s, is the structural answer. Companies with manufacturing capability in the US and Korea — BWXT, Doosan — are the supply-chain bottleneck.

title: Vistra leads nuclear-exposure rally
body: Vistra Energy and Constellation Energy have led nuclear-exposed equities higher this year, with Vistra up over 50% YTD. Cameco has rallied alongside on uranium price strength. Investors are increasingly framing nuclear as part of the broader AI-power thesis.

title: Mag-cap PPAs name nuclear directly — narrative is at consensus
body: When Microsoft and Amazon explicitly cite nuclear in their PPA disclosures, the alpha window for the obvious names is closing. The trade is rotating to second-derivative plays in fuel cycle and reactor components.

title: GLP-1 second-line entrants: Viking and beyond
body: With Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk's GLP-1 supply persistently constrained, second-line entrants like Viking Therapeutics' VK2735 are positioned to capture meaningful share. Phase 2 dual-agonist data has been competitive on weight loss and tolerability. We see VKTX as the cleanest pure-play exposure to the obesity-drug build-out beyond the two incumbents.

title: Why obesity drugs are no longer just a Lilly-Novo story
body: The obesity-drug narrative is shifting. With LLY and NVO priced for perfection, capital is rotating to second-tier challengers and to companion diagnostics. Viking Therapeutics has emerged as the most credible third entrant after positive Phase 2 data. Pharmacogenomics names like GeneDx benefit from polypharmacy concerns as patients combine GLP-1s with other chronic-care drugs.

title: Everyone I know is on Mounjaro now
body: Look around. Half the people in my office are on a GLP-1 drug. The narrative is fully priced into LLY and NVO at this point. The only interesting bets left are diagnostics, oral formulations, and second-tier challengers like VKTX.

title: Oral GLP-1 formulations: the next leg
body: Pfizer's danuglipron stalling in Phase 3 was a setback, but oral GLP-1s remain the holy grail. Whoever lands a tolerable oral formulation first re-rates immediately. VKTX's oral program is ahead of the field on tolerability.

title: Nuclear Energy Will Be Killed By Regulation, Again
body: Single regulatory hearing in Washington and the entire SMR thesis is dead. NRC will never approve any of these reactors. Short the entire complex. (Thread.)
